SELL_CARDS: deprioritised by the owner (2026-11-17), but note it is NOT automatic: this is the in-game sale, an action that costs a turn, and the agent never takes it (100% stop, 319 936 rows). The end-of-game cleanup is a different turn. Revisit when cards are the bottleneck - at 3 MC per card it is the only way to turn a dead card into money while actions still exist.
SELL_CARDS_LAST_ROUND: forced cleanup, not a decision with value: SellExtraCardsState offers it only when player.getNextTurn() == null and the hand is above MAX_HAND_SIZE_LAST_ROUND = 10, at 3 MC per card. The money arrives after the last turn and money is not scored (ScoreBreakdown has no MC term), so the ~9.7 MC it raises per game is dead. The measured +0.18 correlation with the margin is the hand size, not the sale.
MULLIGAN: Measured 18/11 with the afterstate accumulating nothing: the gate called 91.8% of removals 'free' (mean 6.58 discards of 10, clustered at the recording cap) and a deterministic 'hand minus this card' variant 91.6% (mean 9.10). The cause was NOT the random replacement - a random card is worth an average card, not an improvement (owner's correction) - but the engine's queue: the hand is untouched during the loop and the whole set is replaced only at stop, so every step re-scored a full hand and the loop never stopped on its own. A fixed count is not the answer either (0 -> 63.93%, 2 -> 63.75%, 5 -> 60.25% against SMART). The honest afterstep is marginal: step k is 'hand - (queued + candidate) + (k+1) random' against the stop baseline 'hand - queued + k random', same size, so the gap is the value of replacing that one card. This entry stays until that version has been measured.
